constraints: Keep environment.sdk in pubspec.yaml, the sdks block in pubspec.lock, the Flutter version pinned in .fvmrc, and the SDK used in CI on one supported release.
A Flutter project gets its Dart SDK from the Flutter release it pins, so raise the Flutter pin to a release that bundles the Dart version in the replacement instead of installing Dart on its own.

steps.instructions: Change the reported Dart SDK pin to the version in the replacement. For a Flutter project, raise the Flutter version in .fvmrc or .fvm/fvm_config.json to a release that bundles that Dart version.
steps.title: Raise the SDK pin

steps.instructions: Raise the lower bound of environment.sdk in pubspec.yaml (and environment.flutter for an app) so it admits only supported SDKs, then re-resolve dependencies so pubspec.lock records the new sdks constraints.
steps.title: Raise the SDK constraint

steps.instructions: Update CI workflows, Docker images, and setup documentation that install the Dart or Flutter SDK so they match the new pin.
steps.title: Align CI and documentation

verification.purpose: Confirm the active Dart SDK is the intended release.
Re-resolve dependencies against the new SDK constraint.
Analyze and test a Flutter app on the new SDK.
Analyze and test a Dart package on the new SDK.

rule.summary: The Dart security policy commits security updates only for the most recent stable SDK release. Dart 3.8 stopped being that release when Dart 3.9 shipped on 2025-08-13.
rule.title: Dart 3.8 no longer receives security updates
